topics.mining: Use any pickaxe to collect this block. Without a pickaxe it drops nothing. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.location: Find cinnabar in sulfur caves and sulfur springs. Craft or stonecut it into its decorative variants.
topics.operation: Use this mineral material for building and its compatible decorative recipes.

topics.mining: Use any pickaxe to collect this block. Without a pickaxe it drops nothing. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.location: Find sulfur in sulfur caves and sulfur springs. Craft or stonecut it into its decorative variants.
topics.operation: Use this mineral material for building and its compatible decorative recipes.

topics.mining: Use any pickaxe to collect this building shape. Without one it drops nothing. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.location: Craft or stonecut the matching mineral material into slabs, stairs or walls.
topics.water: Single slabs, stairs and walls can be waterlogged.

topics.mining: Use any pickaxe to collect 2 matching slabs. Silk Touch does not keep a double-slab item. Without a pickaxe it drops nothing.
topics.location: Place two matching slabs in one block space.

topics.mining: Use any pickaxe to collect this building shape. Without one it drops nothing. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.location: Craft or stonecut the matching mineral material into slabs, stairs or walls.
topics.water: Single slabs, stairs and walls can be waterlogged.

topics.mining: Use any pickaxe to collect 2 matching slabs. Silk Touch does not keep a double-slab item. Without a pickaxe it drops nothing.
topics.location: Place two matching slabs in one block space.

topics.mining: Use any pickaxe to collect mossy cobblestone. Without a pickaxe it drops nothing.
topics.location: Find mossy cobblestone in monster rooms and other structures, or craft it using cobblestone and a supported moss ingredient.
topics.operation: Mossy cobblestone is decorative masonry. It does not grow or spread moss by itself.

topics.mining: Use any pickaxe to collect this stone building shape. Without a pickaxe it drops nothing.
topics.location: Craft or stonecut the matching stone or masonry material into its building shape.
topics.water: Single slabs, stairs and fences can be waterlogged.

topics.mining: Use a pickaxe to collect 2 matching slabs. Without a pickaxe it drops nothing. Silk Touch does not collect it as a double-slab item.
topics.location: Place 2 matching slabs in the same block space.

topics.mining: Despite its wooden appearance, a petrified oak slab needs a pickaxe to drop as an item.
topics.operation: This is a legacy stone-like slab with an oak appearance, distinct from an ordinary wooden oak slab.
topics.location: Petrified oak slabs are legacy blocks and are not obtained through the ordinary oak slab crafting recipe.

topics.mining: Use any pickaxe to collect smooth stone. Without one it drops nothing.
topics.location: Smelt stone to make smooth stone; smelt cobblestone first if you need stone.
topics.operation: Use smooth stone for construction and compatible recipes, such as blast furnaces and smooth stone slabs.

topics.mining: Use Silk Touch to collect a bee nest with its bees inside. Without Silk Touch the nest drops nothing and bees can emerge angry. An axe is fastest.
topics.location: Look for bee nests on trees in suitable flower-rich Overworld biomes. Growing oak or birch near flowers can also produce nests.
topics.operation: At full honey level, use shears for honeycomb or a bottle for honey. Place a safely positioned lit campfire underneath to calm the bees before harvesting.

topics.mining: A beehive drops itself when broken; an axe is fastest. Silk Touch keeps bees inside. Without it, bees can emerge angry, even though the hive block still drops.
topics.location: Craft a beehive from wooden planks and honeycomb.
topics.operation: A beehive houses up to 3 bees. Harvest a full hive using shears for honeycomb or a bottle for honey, with a safely positioned lit campfire underneath to calm bees.

topics.mining: Silk Touch collects the creaking heart itself. Without Silk Touch it drops 1–3 resin clumps; Fortune can increase those drops.
topics.location: Find creaking hearts inside some naturally generated pale oak trees in pale gardens.
topics.operation: A creaking heart placed between two correctly aligned pale oak logs can activate under the required conditions. Naturally generated hearts link to their creaking; attacking that creaking causes resin to form nearby.

topics.mining: Dried ghasts drop themselves by hand or with any tool. Breaking a waterlogged one resets its hydration progress.
topics.location: Find dried ghasts at Nether fossils in soul sand valleys, or obtain one through its supported recipe or piglin bartering.
topics.growth: Keep a dried ghast waterlogged so it hydrates over time and becomes a ghastling. Removing it from water or breaking it interrupts that progress.

topics.mining: Copper golem statues drop themselves by hand or with any tool; a pickaxe is fastest. They retain their pose.
topics.operation: Use a copper golem statue to change its pose. Scraping a fully oxidized copper golem statue can revive it as a copper golem.
topics.oxidation: Copper statues can oxidize. Honeycomb preserves the current stage; an axe can remove oxidation.

topics.mining: Copper golem statues drop themselves by hand or with any tool; a pickaxe is fastest. They retain their pose.
topics.operation: Use a copper golem statue to change its pose. Scraping a fully oxidized copper golem statue can revive it as a copper golem.
topics.oxidation: Wax keeps the statue at its current stage. Remove wax with an axe before scraping oxidation.

topics.mining: Use any pickaxe to collect a lodestone. Without one it drops nothing.
topics.operation: Use a compass on a lodestone to bind it to that position. The compass points to it in the same dimension; it cannot guide you across dimensions.
topics.location: Craft a lodestone using chiseled stone bricks and an iron ingot, or obtain one from relevant loot.

topics.mining: Use any pickaxe to collect magma blocks. Without one they drop nothing.
topics.location: Look in the Nether and at underwater magma formations in the Overworld.
topics.water: Magma under a column of water source blocks makes a downward bubble column. It can pull swimmers toward the block.
topics.danger: Standing on magma blocks can hurt you. Sneaking helps avoid contact damage, but do not treat a magma bubble column as safe breathing water.

topics.mining: Use a Silk Touch pickaxe to collect nylium. An ordinary pickaxe drops netherrack instead.
topics.location: Find this nylium on the floor of its matching Nether forest biome.
topics.growth: Bone meal on nylium grows Nether vegetation. Bone meal can also spread nearby nylium onto suitable netherrack; keep the growing surface clear.

topics.mining: Use a Silk Touch pickaxe to collect nylium. An ordinary pickaxe drops netherrack instead.
topics.location: Find this nylium on the floor of its matching Nether forest biome.
topics.growth: Bone meal on nylium grows Nether vegetation. Bone meal can also spread nearby nylium onto suitable netherrack; keep the growing surface clear.

topics.mining: Wart blocks drop themselves by hand or with any tool; a hoe is fastest.
topics.location: Find wart blocks in the canopies of matching huge Nether fungi.
topics.operation: Use wart blocks for building. A Nether wart block cannot be crafted back into Nether wart items.

topics.mining: Shroomlights drop themselves by hand or with any tool; a hoe is fastest.
topics.location: Find shroomlights in the canopies of huge crimson and warped fungi, including fungi grown with bone meal.
topics.operation: Shroomlights give steady light without needing fuel or redstone power.

topics.mining: Froglights drop themselves by hand or with any tool. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.location: Have a temperate frog eat a tiny magma cube to produce this froglight.
topics.operation: Froglights are steady light blocks. They do not need redstone power.

topics.mining: Froglights drop themselves by hand or with any tool. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.location: Have a cold frog eat a tiny magma cube to produce this froglight.
topics.operation: Froglights are steady light blocks. They do not need redstone power.

topics.mining: Froglights drop themselves by hand or with any tool. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.location: Have a warm frog eat a tiny magma cube to produce this froglight.
topics.operation: Froglights are steady light blocks. They do not need redstone power.

topics.mining: Sea pickles drop themselves by hand or with any tool. A cluster gives the number of pickles it contains.
topics.location: Find sea pickles in warm-ocean coral reefs.
topics.growth: Use bone meal on a sea pickle underwater on live coral to grow more pickles nearby. They emit light only while underwater.

topics.mining: Use shears to collect glow lichen. Ordinary tools, including Silk Touch tools without shears, do not collect it.
topics.location: Look for glow lichen on cave surfaces in the Overworld.
topics.growth: Use bone meal to spread glow lichen over adjacent suitable faces.

topics.mining: Break this plant by hand or with any tool to collect it. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.location: Look in cherry groves.
topics.growth: Place it on suitable soil. Bone meal can produce additional plants or expand the patch, depending on the plant.

topics.mining: Break this plant by hand or with any tool to collect it. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.location: Look in birch forests and meadows.
topics.growth: Place it on suitable soil. Bone meal can produce additional plants or expand the patch, depending on the plant.

topics.mining: Break this plant by hand or with any tool to collect it. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.location: Look in swamps and beside some rivers.
topics.growth: Place it on suitable soil. Bone meal can produce additional plants or expand the patch, depending on the plant.

topics.mining: Break this plant by hand or with any tool to collect it. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.location: Look in appropriate grassy Overworld biomes.
topics.growth: Place it on suitable soil. Bone meal can produce additional plants or expand the patch, depending on the plant.

topics.mining: Break the plant by hand or with any tool to collect it.
topics.location: Look for this plant in the tops of suitable tall cactus plants.
topics.operation: This is a decorative plant, not a crop that repeatedly produces food.

topics.mining: Break the plant by hand or with any tool to collect it.
topics.location: Look for this plant in lush-cave ceilings.
topics.operation: This is a decorative plant, not a crop that repeatedly produces food.

topics.mining: Break the plant by hand or with any tool to collect it.
topics.location: Look for this plant in grown torchflower crops.
topics.operation: This is a decorative plant, not a crop that repeatedly produces food.

topics.mining: Break the plant by hand or with any tool to collect it.
topics.location: Look for this plant in grown pitcher crops.
topics.operation: This is a decorative plant, not a crop that repeatedly produces food.

topics.mining: Break the plant by hand or with any tool to collect it.
topics.location: Look for this plant in locations where a Wither kills a suitable mob.
topics.operation: Wither roses inflict Wither on vulnerable entities touching them. Handle and place them carefully.

topics.mining: Use shears to collect this plant. Otherwise it drops sticks or nothing.
topics.location: Look for this plant in deserts and badlands.
topics.operation: This is a decorative plant, not a crop that repeatedly produces food.

topics.mining: Use shears to collect this plant. Otherwise it drops sticks or nothing.
topics.location: Look for this plant in warped forests.
topics.operation: This is a decorative plant, not a crop that repeatedly produces food.

topics.mining: Eyeblossoms drop themselves when broken by hand or with any tool.
topics.location: Find eyeblossoms in pale gardens.
topics.growth: Eyeblossoms open at night and close during the day under normal conditions. Bone meal can produce another matching flower.

topics.mining: Use Silk Touch to collect turtle eggs. Breaking them normally or trampling them destroys them without a drop.
topics.location: Breed turtles with seagrass so a pregnant turtle returns to its home beach to lay eggs.
topics.growth: Place turtle eggs on sand or red sand to hatch. They hatch more quickly at night; protect them from trampling and egg-breaking mobs.

topics.mining: Sniffer eggs drop themselves even by hand. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.location: Brush suspicious sand in warm ocean ruins for a chance of a sniffer egg, or breed sniffers.
topics.growth: Place a sniffer egg to hatch. Placing it on moss makes it hatch faster.

topics.mining: Frogspawn cannot be collected in normal Survival, even with Silk Touch. Breaking it destroys it.
topics.location: Breed two frogs with slimeballs; one lays frogspawn on nearby suitable water.
topics.growth: Leave frogspawn on suitable water and wait for tadpoles to hatch. Collect tadpoles with a water bucket rather than trying to collect the frogspawn.

topics.mining: Breaking an item frame drops the frame. Remove its displayed item first if you want to keep that item separate.
topics.operation: Use an item frame to display an item or map. Interact to rotate the displayed item; glow frames make the display appear bright.
topics.redstone: A comparator can read an item frame and use its item rotation to produce different output strengths.

topics.mining: A shovel collects snowballs from snow layers. Use a Silk Touch shovel to collect the snow layer instead.
topics.location: Find snow layers on cold-biome terrain after snowfall.
topics.operation: Snow layers are thin ground coverings, distinct from full snow blocks and powder snow.

topics.mining: Frosted ice cannot be collected, even with Silk Touch. It is temporary ice created by Frost Walker.
topics.location: Walk near suitable water while wearing Frost Walker boots to create temporary frosted ice.
topics.operation: Frosted ice melts back into water. Use ordinary ice or packed ice when you need a lasting building material.

topics.mining: Dirt paths drop dirt, not a path block, even with Silk Touch. A shovel is fastest.
topics.location: Use a shovel on suitable dirt-like ground to make a path. Villages also contain paths.
topics.operation: Dirt paths are slightly lower walking surfaces. Placing a solid block directly above can turn the path back into dirt.

topics.mining: Break placed redstone dust by hand or with any tool to collect the dust.
topics.operation: Place redstone dust on supported surfaces to connect circuit components. Signal strength decreases as it travels along dust.
topics.redstone: Redstone dust carries signal strengths from 0 to 15. Use repeaters to restore strength on longer lines.
